sources.title: The Secret History of the Mongols (c. 1228) -- the earliest surviving Mongolian-language chronicle, written within Mongol court circles
Jack Weatherford, Genghis Khan and the Making of the Modern World (2004) -- independent modern scholarship

systems_abstraction.rationale: Assigned administrative/military responsibilities based on individual ability and loyalty rather than kinship (a departure from standard steppe kin-based court practice); restructured Mongol society into a decimal military-administrative system (units of ten/hundred/thousand) that deliberately dispersed defeated groups across units rather than keeping tribal structures intact, credited with preventing the empire's fragmentation along old tribal lines even after his death (Weatherford; Wikipedia).

independent_thinking.rationale: Departed from the standard steppe practice of kin-based court appointment in favor of ability/loyalty-based assignment (Weatherford).

planning_orientation.rationale: The decimal military-administrative reorganization was a deliberate, structural redesign of Mongol society, not an improvised response (Wikipedia, existing verified finding).

persistence.rationale: After a military defeat at the Battle of Qalaqaljid Sands, retreated to Baljuna and rebuilt his coalition from a small group of companions (the 1203 Baljuna Covenant) rather than abandoning the campaign; sustained a rivalry with Jamukha across roughly a decade before finally prevailing in 1206.

risk_tolerance.rationale: In 1219, after the Khwarazmian governor of Otrar executed a Mongol trade caravan and Shah Muhammad II executed/mutilated the envoys sent to demand redress, launched a full invasion of the much larger, settled Khwarazmian state (existing verified finding).

decisiveness.rationale: At about 14, ambushed and killed his half-brother Behter after Behter withheld hunting spoils from him and his brother Qasar (The Secret History of the Mongols); after Jamukha's own followers betrayed him in 1206, executed the betrayers specifically on the stated principle that betrayal merits the harshest punishment; launched the 1219 Khwarazmian invasion in direct, immediate response to the Otrar incident.

collaboration.rationale: The 1203 Baljuna Covenant united a small group of companions from nine different tribes across Christian, Muslim, and Buddhist faiths on loyalty to him and each other after a shared defeat -- a real but narrowly loyalty-bound alliance, not a general collaborative disposition.

leadership_drive.rationale: Built and sustained the Baljuna coalition, the ability/loyalty-based appointment system, and the decimal reorganization -- three distinct, deliberate institution-building efforts rather than a single moment of command.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Killed his own half-brother Behter over a resource dispute (Secret History); sustained roughly a decade of open rivalry with his former anda Jamukha; launched and sustained the large-scale, multi-year Khwarazmian campaign following the Otrar incident.

competitiveness.rationale: The Behter killing (a dispute over hunting spoils with an older half-brother) and the sustained, decade-long rivalry with Jamukha (culminating in Jamukha's own claim that "there was room for only one Mongol lord") both reflect direct, personal rivalry rather than only strategic calculation.

autonomy_need.rationale: Executed Jamukha's betrayers on his own stated principle rather than simply accepting their offered service; broke from standard kin-based court convention in his appointment practices (Weatherford).

opportunity_sensing.rationale: Early unification exploited shifting tribal alliances (Merkit/Tatar/Kerait/Naiman) at a specific fragile political moment -- recognizing which openings to act on before committing, distinct from adaptability (adjusting an already-chosen course).

proactive_agency.rationale: Rebuilt alliances and pursued unification entirely on his own initiative after his clan abandoned his family following his father's death, with no inherited authority or assigned role at that stage; the 1203 Baljuna retreat-and-rebuild after a battlefield defeat is a further instance of the same self-directed pattern.

portrait.attribution: Yuan dynasty imperial portrait album, c.1350, National Palace Museum, Taipei -- a posthumous portrait painted roughly 120+ years after Genghis Khan's death, part of a Yuan court ancestor-portrait tradition, not a lifetime or eyewitness likeness

provenance.notes: Legacy integrity remediation batch 5 (2026-09-14, docs/checkpoints/legacy-integrity-batch5-three-person-remediation.md), using the unchanged deterministic risk-triage methodology from batches 2-4, corrected in batch 4 to use the true 30-attribute base set (belief_updating is taxonomy_v1.1, not base). Genghis Khan ranked #1 among 25 legacy profiles with risk score 10 (tied with serena-williams, alphabetically first): 1 source cited, 20 high-confidence rows in the unsupported base set, 2 'documented'-tier claims among them, no Wikidata QID, era medieval with >=15 high-confidence base rows. New research (The Secret History of the Mongols and Jack Weatherford's independent modern scholarship) audited all 22 original rows (20 base + 2 taxonomy_v1.1). 13 retained and rescored from the evidence directly (none reusing old values), 0 new rows added, 9 removed for lacking individually-attributable, non-duplicative support this cycle (analytical_rigor, discipline, execution_speed, adaptability, ambiguity_tolerance, social_assertiveness, persuasiveness, achievement_drive, impact_motivation). achievement_drive/impact_motivation were removed specifically because the only support behind them was the scale of his conquests/empire (achievement/output), not a distinct behavioral incident, per this project's standing rule. This is a political/military-primary-identity legacy profile audited on identical evidentiary terms as every other target in this lane, per this cycle's explicit instruction to keep product-selection policy (the newer zero-politics cohort-selection standard for NEW candidates) separate from legacy data-integrity auditing. The 1219 Khwarazmian invasion and the 1206 execution of Behter are reported factually as documented behavioral incidents, not moralized, and not assigned a specific casualty figure given this profile's existing, still-valid caveat about unreliable/hostile-chronicle sourcing for casualty claims. His father's murder and his family's subsequent abandonment/childhood hardship were read but not used as row evidence -- only his own later, independently documented actions (rebuilding alliances, the Baljuna Covenant) were used, consistent with this project's standing health/tragedy/circumstance discipline. Publication decision (evidence_approved) was frozen before eligibility_v2 was computed.
